definition.interpretation: The observed divergence ratio of 1.028 suggests that interaction-coupling between agents successfully restricts variance, consistent with the canalization hypothesis. This finding supports the premise that state-space dependencies stabilize value trajectories against random amplification.
definition.limitations: The sample size and coupling mechanism are simplified; results may not generalize to higher-dimensional or non-linear state spaces.
definition.next_step: Define a new experiment with variable coupling strengths to test if canalization persists or collapses under high perturbation.

definition.cost: Minimal computational overhead; consistent with existing resource allocation.
definition.reason: Initial tests show supporting evidence for the canalization model, but behavior at boundary conditions remains untested.
definition.stop_condition: Failure to demonstrate constrained variance across three distinct coupling strengths.
definition.uncertainty: The stability limit of canalization under high coupling variation is unknown.

definition.reason: Experimental validation of boundary conditions is required to strengthen the canalization hypothesis.
definition.stop: Completion of planned parameter variation tests.
definition.uncertainty: Unclear if canalization is a robust universal feature or specific to current parameter ranges.

proposal.summary: Reviewed experiment exp-divergent-values-test-78, which showed that interaction-coupling constrains variance (divergence ratio 1.028, within tolerance 1.1). Interpretation suggests that canalization effectively limits value divergence in the tested system. Proceeding with refinement of the hypothesis to explore the limits of this stabilization under higher coupling variance.
proposal.title: Analysis of Interaction Coupling and Value Canalization
